business.description: SWELECT Energy Systems Limited is a public listed company and a leading player in India's renewable energy sector with over four decades of expertise in clean power, power electronics, solar solutions and integrated energy systems. The company has evolved from a trusted UPS and power conditioning solutions company into a future-ready renewable energy enterprise delivering Solar, Wind, Energy Storage Systems, IPP, EPC for corporates, industries, government customers, residential users and commercial establishments.

outlook.statement: Objective to expand IPP portfolio to approximately 1 GW over the next two years while simultaneously strengthening EPC business and expanding rooftop and channel distribution businesses
Expect to launch commercial and industrial BESS solutions with hybrid inverters during Q2 FY27
Will commission a 10 MWh BESS system at SHPV manufacturing facility in Coimbatore during the year
Pursue selective opportunities through FortifyGrid partnership in US market
Expand rooftop and channel distribution businesses
Develop integrated renewable energy solutions combining solar, wind and storage
Maintain disciplined capital allocation focussed on improving returns and shareholder value
Ambitious roadmap to build a 1 GW IPP portfolio over the next two years across solar, hybrid renewable energy and energy storage projects to deliver round-the-clock clean power solutions.

Move from preparation to execution in BESS: commercial launch of residential and C&I solutions following certification approvals, scaling successful pilot projects into standardised offerings, increasing participation in utility-scale tenders, operationalising the United States joint venture, strengthening engineering, procurement and project delivery capabilities.
SHPV expansion underway to achieve manufacturing capacity of 2 GW.
Actively pursuing major BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) and hybrid tenders, engineering 100+ MWh utility-scale BESS and hybrid solutions, with a roadmap for Round-the-Clock (RTC) solutions
The Company is exploring various strategic opportunities to commence its business activity

Accelerated push into EPC, IPP, BESS and channel markets alongside continued investment in manufacturing excellence at SHPV; targeting 1 GW cumulative EPC target and 1 GW IPP solar asset portfolio; launching BESS products through channel partner network across Tier 1, 2, and 3 markets; pursuing hybrid solar-plus-BESS EPC mandates under SECI and state-level RTC tenders; active expansion planned across North India.
PVEL extended reliability certification completion expected in FY 2026-27.
Residential BESS portfolio (3 kW to 300 kW solar hybrid inverters under SWELECT brand) currently undergoing BIS certification.
India's 500 GW non-fossil fuel target by 2030 requires approximately 160 GW of additional solar capacity over the next four years; FY 2025-26 added a record 44 GW.
SHPV's 2 GW capacity expansion expected to be commissioned by July 2026, positioning it to serve domestic utility-scale, C&I, and export markets at significantly greater scale.
Targeting at least 500 MW PPAs by March 2027 for IPP portfolio; pipeline of more than 150 MW PPAs being pursued and expected to be signed by Q1 FY 2026-27.
Channels Division intends to at least double revenue in FY 2026-27; deeper digital enablement of channel partners, expansion of BESS distribution, growing penetration into Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.

BESS priorities: commercial launch of residential and C&I offerings post-certification; scaling pilots into standardized, repeatable solutions; expanding utility-scale tender participation; operationalizing the U.S. joint venture; strengthening engineering, procurement, and project delivery capabilities.
India BESS market valued at USD 1.54 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 8.59 billion by 2031 at 33.2% CAGR; CEA estimates 47 GW or 236 GWh BESS capacity needed by 2032.
TOPCon-first strategy through 2028–2030, PVEL certification, and expanding R&D programme
Management expects that approximately 100% of the transaction price allocated to the unsatisfied contracts as of 31 March 2026 will be recognised as revenue next year.

The Group has revisited the projections made in the previous year taking into account the probable beneficial results arising from the various initiatives being undertaken with regard to restructure of the customer contracts, submission and pursuing with appropriate authorities on relevant claims.

The Management has concluded that the carrying value of the property, plant and equipment and intangible assets are recoverable duly considering the expected future recoverable value as at 31 March 2026.
